0|57bbf99ce9639c46eec43081d30e2763c135c653|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"dm integrity: Use alloc_ordered_workqueue() to create ordered workqueues
BACKGROUND
When multiple work items are queued to a workqueue
doesn't match the queueing order. They may get executed in any order and
simultaneously. When fully serialized execution - one by one in the queueing
order - is needed
column2: an ordered workqueue should be used which can be created

column1: with alloc_ordered_workqueue().
However
column2: alloc_ordered_workqueue() was a later addition. Before it

column1: ordered workqueue could be obtained by creating an UNBOUND workqueue with
@max_active==1. This originally was an implementation side-effect which was
broken by 4c16bd327c74 (""workqueue: restore WQ_UNBOUND/max_active==1 to be
ordered""). Because there were users that depended on the ordered execution
5c0338c68706 (""workqueue: restore WQ_UNBOUND/max_active==1 to be ordered"")
made workqueue allocation path to implicitly promote UNBOUND workqueues w/
@max_active==1 to ordered workqueues.
While this has worked okay
this way creates other issues. It's difficult to tell whether a given
workqueue actually needs to be ordered and users that legitimately want a
min concurrency level wq unexpectedly gets an ordered one instead. With
planned UNBOUND workqueue updates to improve execution locality and more
prevalence of chiplet designs which can benefit from such improvements
isn't a state we wanna be in forever.
This patch series audits all callsites that create an UNBOUND workqueue w/
@max_active==1 and converts them to alloc_ordered_workqueue() as necessary.
WHAT TO LOOK FOR
The conversions are from
alloc_workqueue(WQ_UNBOUND | flags
to
alloc_ordered_workqueue(flags
which don't cause any functional changes. If you know that fully ordered
execution is not necessary
column2: please let me know. I'll drop the conversion and

column1: instead add a comment noting the fact to reduce confusion while conversion
is in progress.
If you aren't fully sure
column2: it's completely fine to let the conversion

column1: through. The behavior will stay exactly the same and we can always
reconsider later.
As there are follow-up workqueue core changes
patch can be routed through the workqueue tree w/ your acks. Thanks.
